This folder is the Breezell plugin `{{id}}` ({{displayName}}): a VS Code extension whose `package.json`
has a `breezell` object and which uses `vscode.breezell`.

Before changing anything, read `.agents/skills/breezell-plugin/SKILL.md`, then the reference page in

`types/breezell.d.ts`.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `npm install` | Install the tools |
| `npm run build` / `npm run watch` | Build `src/` into `dist/` (not in a Pack: it has no code) |
| `npm run typecheck` | Type check (not in a Pack) |
| `npm run validate` | Check `package.json` as Breezell reads it |
| `npm run package:open` / `package:closed` | Pack a `.vsix` |

# {{displayName}}

{{description}}

A [Breezell](https://breezell.com) plugin (`{{id}}`).

## Develop

```bash
npm install
```

Open this folder in Breezell and press **F5**: the plugin runs in a development window.
Plugins run only while you are signed in to Breezell.

- `src/extension.ts` — the plugin. Besides the VS Code API it can use `vscode.breezell`
  (typings in `types/breezell.d.ts`); ask only for the permissions you need in
  `package.json` › `breezell.permissions`.
- `npm run validate` — check `package.json`.

## Package

```bash
npm run package:open     # open source: the source ships in the package
npm run package:closed   # closed source: minified build only, no source
```

Either command writes `{{id}}-<version>.vsix`. Install it in Breezell from
**Plugins › Installed › Install local .vsix**. It works without uploading it anywhere.

## Publish to the Breezell plugin market

1. Fork [BreezellCode/BreezellCode](https://github.com/BreezellCode/BreezellCode) and clone your fork.
2. `node tools/breezell-plugin.mjs submit --market <path to your clone>`
3. Commit, push and open a pull request. The market check runs on it.

Guide: <https://github.com/BreezellCode/BreezellCode/tree/main/plugins>

# Breezell plugins

A Breezell plugin is a VS Code extension whose `package.json` has a `breezell` object. It can use the
whole VS Code API, and `vscode.breezell` for what is Breezell's, limited to the permissions it declares.
Work in this order: understand the request, choose permissions, declare, write code, check, test, pack.
Read the reference page for the part you touch before writing it: they are short and exact.

## 1. Look before you change anything

- `package.json`: the `breezell` object (`apiVersion`, `permissions`, `optionalPermissions`, `source`) and
  `contributes.breezell`.
- `types/breezell.d.ts`: the API this project can call. When a call you need is missing, the copy is old:
  replace it, and `tools/breezell-plugin.mjs` with it, from
  `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BreezellCode/BreezellCode/main/plugins/devkit/breezell.d.ts` and
  `.../devkit/breezell-plugin.mjs`. The pages in `references/` are copies of the market's `plugins/docs`:
  the newest are at `https://github.com/BreezellCode/BreezellCode/tree/main/plugins/docs`.
- `src/extension.ts` (none in a Pack) and the scripts in `package.json`.

## 2. From what the user wants to what to use

| The user wants | Permission | Use | Read |
|---|---|---|---|
| Use their chat model (or another of the picker's) | `models.request` | `models.request` | `references/models.md` |
| Know when the AI starts or finishes, no content | `chat.events` (normal) | `chat.onDidStartTurn`, `onDidFinishTurn` | `references/chat.md` |
| Read conversations, tool calls, recalled memories | `chat.read` | `listConversations`, `getConversation`, `onDidChangeConversation` | `references/chat.md` |
| Send messages, start conversations, stop a reply, keep work going | `chat.send` | `chat.send`, `chat.stop`, `holdDoneNotice` | `references/chat.md` |
| Approve or reject a waiting tool call | `chat.approve` | `chat.approve`, `chat.reject` | `references/chat.md` |
| Change, stop or add context to what the user sends | `chat.intercept` | `chat.registerSendHandler` | `references/chat.md` |
| Read the chat box | `chat.input` | `chat.readInput` | `references/chat.md` |
| Give the agent a tool | `agent.tools` | `contributes.breezell.tools` + `tools.register` | `references/agent.md` |
| See or refuse the agent's tool calls | `agent.hooks` | `tools.registerCallHandler`, `tools.onDidRunTool` | `references/agent.md` |
| Skills, rules, MCP servers with no code | none (`agent.tools` for MCP) | `contributes.breezell.skills`, `rules`, `mcpServers` | `references/agent.md` |
| Buttons, slash menu rows, pages, modes, settings cards | `ui.contribute` (normal) | `contributes.breezell.ui` | `references/ui.md` |
| Hide, move, restyle or replace Breezell's parts; colours, fonts, a stylesheet; a companion | `ui.modify` | `contributes.breezell.ui` | `references/ui.md` |
| Draw a code fence language | `chat.render` | `ui.renderers` | `references/ui.md` |
| A window of its own, also without the editor | none | `contributes.breezell.windows` + `windows.open` | `references/windows.md` |
| The model picker | `models.select` (normal) | `models.list`, `models.select` | `references/models.md` |
| Custom APIs without keys / with keys | `providers.list` (normal) / `providers.read` | `providers.list` / `providers.listCustom` | `references/models.md` |
| A restart | `app.restart` (normal), `app.forceRestart` | `app.requestRestart`, `contributes.breezell.restart` | `references/restart.md` |

Every permission: `references/permissions.md`. Every call: `references/api.md`. Errors: `references/errors.md`.
Limits: `references/limits.md`. Whole examples to start from: `references/recipes.md`.

## 3. Rules that hold everywhere

- **Fewest permissions.** Declare only what the code uses. A permission newer than the user's Breezell
  refuses the install from `permissions`: put new ones (`agent.hooks`, `providers.list`, ...) in
  `optionalPermissions` and check `vscode.breezell.permissions` before using them.
- **Expect refusals.** Dangerous permissions are asked at first use and can be turned off any time. Catch
  errors, check `error.name` (`BreezellPermissionDenied`, `BreezellNotSignedIn`, ...), and tell the user what
  the plugin cannot do. Never retry in a loop.
- **Check for the API.** `vscode.breezell` is undefined outside Breezell; plugins run only while signed in.
- **Declare, do not inject.** Breezell's own window runs no plugin script or CSS. Change its screens only
  through `contributes.breezell.ui` (or a stylesheet, which is read as declarations); a plugin's own UI goes
  in a page (`ui.surfaces`), a webview or a window.
- **Never touch** Breezell's internal commands (`breezell.*`), its sign-in, plan, quota, custom API,
  approvals or errors, or its files (sign-ins, conversations, memories). Never imitate its sign-in or
  payment screens or work around billing. These are refused, and review rejects plugins that try.
- **Private data stays put.** What `chat.read`, `chat.input`, `chat.intercept`, `agent.hooks` and agent tools
  hand over stays on the user's computer unless the README says where it goes. Keys from `providers.listCustom`
  go only to their provider. Secrets go in `context.secrets`.
- **Be quick where Breezell waits.** A send handler or tool call handler that takes over 3 seconds is passed
  over. Do slow work before or after, not in them.
- **Start with Breezell** (`"activationEvents": ["onStartupFinished"]`) when registering tools, a send handler
  or a tool call handler: nothing is offered before the code is registered.
- **Remote windows:** `"extensionKind": ["ui", "workspace"]`.
- **Market text is English:** README, package.json texts, commit messages. Translations go in `i18n/`
  (`references/translations.md`).

## 4. Before saying it is done

1. `npm run validate`: no problems. Everything it reports, Breezell would leave out.
2. `npm run typecheck`: no errors (a Pack has no code and no such script).
3. `npm run build`: it builds (not in a Pack).
4. Each permission is used and explained in the README; each call's errors are handled.
5. Tell the user how to try it: open the folder in Breezell, press **F5**, sign in in the development window,
   and what to do there. Say which permissions Breezell will ask for.
6. To install it for real: `npm run package:open` (or `package:closed`), then **Plugins › Installed › Install
   local .vsix**. To publish: `references/publishing.md`.

## 5. Mistakes seen often

- A turn event's `conversationId` is not the id of `listConversations`: use `chat.conversationOfTurn(turnId)`.
- An `automated` message after the user pressed Stop fails with `BreezellStoppedByUser` until they write again.
- `chat.send` refuses a conversation that is busy; wait for `onDidFinishTurn`.
- `models.request` runs at most 2 at a time and 20 a minute per plugin.
- Tool parameters and results from `chat.read` are cut at 20,000 characters (`resultLength` is the real length).
- A must-read colour pair (`send-bg`/`send-fg`, `approve-*`, `reject-*`, `error-*`, `accent`/`accent-fg`) is used
  only when both are written out, opaque and contrast at least 4.5.
- A setting a look follows (`when`, `variants`, a token `{ "setting" }`) must be the plugin's own, in
  `contributes.configuration`.
- Values crossing to Breezell are JSON: no functions, class instances or `Date` objects.

## References

All in `references/`, the same pages as the market's `plugins/docs`:

`README.md` (index), `getting-started.md`, `manifest.md`, `permissions.md`, `api.md`, `errors.md`, `limits.md`,
`chat.md`, `models.md`, `agent.md`, `ui.md`, `windows.md`, `restart.md`, `translations.md`, `security.md`,
`publishing.md`, `recipes.md`.

# Breezell plugin documentation

Everything you need to build a Breezell plugin, from the first command to the market. The
[market overview](https://github.com/BreezellCode/BreezellCode/blob/main/plugins/README.md) is the short version; these pages are the whole of it. They are also
the reference of the AI skill every new plugin ships with (see [Working with an AI assistant](#working-with-an-ai-assistant)).

Typings: [`devkit/breezell.d.ts`](https://github.com/BreezellCode/BreezellCode/blob/main/plugins/devkit/breezell.d.ts)
(in a plugin made from a template: `types/breezell.d.ts`).

## Read in this order

| Page | What it covers |
|---|---|
| [Getting started](getting-started.md) | Make a plugin, run it, check it, pack it, install it |
| [package.json](manifest.md) | The `breezell` object, `contributes.breezell`, how a plugin opens |
| [Permissions](permissions.md) | Every permission, which are asked for, what each gives |
| [API reference](api.md) | Every call of `vscode.breezell`, with its permission and limits |
| [Errors](errors.md) | What each error name means and what to do |
| [Limits](limits.md) | Every limit in one table |

## By topic

| Page | What it covers |
|---|---|
| [The chat](chat.md) | Turn events, reading conversations, sending, stopping, work over many turns, a message before it is sent |
| [Models and providers](models.md) | The user's models: requests, streaming, images, JSON; the model picker; custom APIs |
| [The agent](agent.md) | Packs (skills, rules, MCP servers), agent tools, watching and refusing the agent's tool calls |
| [Breezell's screens](ui.md) | Buttons, the slash menu, pages, a companion, settings, patches, tokens, fonts, a stylesheet, variants, code fences, modes |
| [Windows](windows.md) | Windows of the plugin's own, also without an editor |
| [Restarting Breezell](restart.md) | Asking for a restart, after an install or an update too |
| [Translations](translations.md) | The README, name, description and commands in other languages |
| [Security](security.md) | What plugins cannot reach, and what users and review expect |
| [Publishing](publishing.md) | Open or closed source, the market, review, the blocklist |
| [Recipes](recipes.md) | Whole small plugins for common tasks |

## Versions

A plugin declares the API generation it was written for in `breezell.apiVersion` (1). Breezell adds to
generation 1 without breaking it; pages mark what needs a newer Breezell. A permission an older Breezell
does not know refuses the install when it is in `permissions`, so put new ones in `optionalPermissions`
and check `vscode.breezell.permissions` (or a call's error) before using them. Fields an older Breezell
does not know in `contributes.breezell` are ignored, so declaring them is safe.

## Working with an AI assistant

Every plugin made from a template (in Breezell or with `breezell-plugin.mjs init`) has:

- `.agents/skills/breezell-plugin/`: a skill with the workflow, the rules and these pages as its
  references. Breezell's own agent finds it in the plugin's folder, as do tools that read `.agents/skills`.
- `AGENTS.md`, and `CLAUDE.md` pointing to it: what any assistant should read first.

Ask the assistant for what you want ("a panel that lists the files the agent changed"); the skill tells it
which permissions that needs, which calls to use, and to run `npm run validate` and `npm run typecheck`
before it says it is done. The same pages are here for you to read.

# API reference

Every member of `vscode.breezell`, with the permission it needs. The typings are
[`breezell.d.ts`](https://github.com/BreezellCode/BreezellCode/blob/main/plugins/devkit/breezell.d.ts)
(in a plugin made from a template: `types/breezell.d.ts`); this page says what the typings cannot.

`vscode.breezell` is `undefined` in other editors and in Breezell versions without the plugin API, so
check it first. A call fails with an `Error` whose `name` says why ([Errors](errors.md)): check the name,
not the message, which may change.

```ts
const breezell = vscode.breezell;
if (!breezell) {
	return; // not Breezell
}
try {
	await breezell.chat.send('Hello');
} catch (error) {
	if ((error as Error).name === 'BreezellPermissionDenied') { /* say what the plugin cannot do */ }
}
```

## Top level

| Member | Permission | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `apiVersion` | none | The API generation this Breezell implements (`1`) |
| `permissions` | none | The permissions this plugin declared (with the optional ones this Breezell knows) |
| `permissionState(p)` | declared `p` | `granted`, `denied` or `ask`; asks no one |
| `requestPermission(p)` | declared `p` | Asks the user when it is the first time; whether it is allowed |
| `onDidChangePermissions` | none | The user changed one of this plugin's permissions (after one of the two calls above) |
| `language`, `onDidChangeLanguage` | none | Breezell's display language: `en`, `zh-CN`, `zh-TW`, `ja`, `ko`, `ru`, `es`, `pt-BR`. `vscode.env.language` does not follow it. Empty for a moment at start |

## `account`

| Member | Permission | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `isSignedIn`, `onDidChangeSignIn` | none | Whether a Breezell account is signed in. Plugins run only while one is |

## `app`

| Member | Permission | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `requestRestart({ scope, reason, l10n, force })` | `app.restart`; `app.forceRestart` with `force` | Ask to restart `extensionHost`, `window` or `app`, or with `force` restart without asking (once per plugin version). `true` when it will happen. See [Restarting Breezell](restart.md) |

## `chat`

| Member | Permission | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `onDidStartTurn`, `onDidFinishTurn` | `chat.events` | `{ turnId, conversationId, mode }`; a finish adds `outcome` (`completed`, `error`, `stopped`) and `durationMs`. No content |
| `conversationOfTurn(turnId)` | `chat.read` | The `listConversations` id of a turn event's conversation; undefined for a turn too long ago (the last 200 are kept) |
| `listConversations()` | `chat.read` | This workspace's conversations, most recently changed first: `id`, `title`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `messageCount`, `current`, `activity`, `backgroundCommands` |
| `getConversation(id)` | `chat.read` | The same with `messages`, `streaming` and `usage` |
| `onDidChangeConversation` | `chat.read` | `{ conversationId, activity, streaming, backgroundCommands }`, at most every 150 ms per conversation |
| `show(id)` | `chat.read` | Opens the conversation in Breezell's chat |
| `readInput()` | `chat.input` | The chat box: `text`, `before` (before the caret), `recent` (last messages' text) |
| `registerSendHandler(handler)` | `chat.intercept` | See each message the user sends before it goes: change it, stop it, add context for the AI. One per plugin. See [A message before it is sent](chat.md#a-message-before-it-is-sent) |
| `send(text, options)` | `chat.send` | Send as the user would: `conversationId` (none: a new one), `automated`, `mode`, `model`, `attachments`. Resolves to `{ conversationId }` once the message is in |
| `stop(id)` | `chat.send` | Stops the reply being written; not the user's Stop |
| `holdDoneNotice(id)`, `releaseDoneNotice(id, { announce })` | `chat.send` | No done sound or notification until released. See [Work over many turns](chat.md#work-over-many-turns) |
| `approve(id)`, `reject(id)` | `chat.approve` | Answer the tool call the conversation waits for |

### Conversation messages

`getConversation(id).messages` is what the chat shows, in order; `index` is the row's position.

| `kind` | Fields |
|---|---|
| `user` | `text`, `time`, `attachments` (names), `recalledMemories` (`id`, `summary`, `detail`, `priority`, `source`), `memoryUse` (`resident`, `relevant`, `complete`, `inThisConversation`), `automatedBy` (a plugin's message: `{ id, name }`) |
| `assistant` | `text`, `reasoning`, `usage` (`inputTokens`, `outputTokens`, `cacheReadTokens`, `cacheWriteTokens`) |
| `tool` | `id`, `name`, `status` (`invalid`, `awaitingApproval`, `running`, `done`, `failed`, `rejected`), `params`, `result` (cut at 20,000 characters), `resultLength`, `mcpServer`, `plugin` (`{ id, name }` for a plugin's tool) |
| `error` | `text` |

`usage` on a conversation adds `replies` and `repliesWithoutUsage`. Token counts are the provider's, for a
budget of your own: some providers count cache reads inside `inputTokens`, and subagents are not included.

## `models`

| Member | Permission | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `list()` | `models.select` | The model picker's models: `provider`, `model`, `name`, `current` |
| `select({ provider, model })` | `models.select` | Switches the chat model to one of them |
| `request(request, token)` | `models.request` | A request to the chat model or `request.model`: `messages` (`role`, `content`, `images`), `system`, `model`, `responseFormat: 'json'`, `maxOutputTokens`, `onText`, `onReasoning`. Answers `{ text, model, usage, json }`. See [Models and providers](models.md) |

## `providers`

| Member | Permission | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `list()` | `providers.list` | Custom APIs without keys: `id`, `name`, `protocol`, `host`, `headerNames`, `poolAccounts`, `models` (`id`, `enabled`, `current`) |
| `listCustom()` | `providers.read` | Custom APIs as their settings page shows them, API keys included; plan with Custom API only |

## `tools`

| Member | Permission | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `register(name, { invoke })` | `agent.tools` | The code of a tool declared in `contributes.breezell.tools`. See [Agent tools](agent.md#agent-tools) |
| `registerCallHandler(handler)` | `agent.hooks` | See each tool call of the agent before it runs and refuse it: answer `{ deny: true, reason }`. One per plugin. See [The agent's tool calls](agent.md#the-agents-tool-calls) |
| `onDidRunTool` | `agent.hooks` | A call the plugins were asked about finished: the call with `status` (`done`, `failed`, `rejected`), `result`, `resultLength` |

## `ui`

| Member | Permission | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `onDidOpenSurface` | none (the page is declared) | One of the plugin's pages opened: `surfaceId`, `context`, `postMessage(m)`, `onDidReceiveMessage`, `onDidClose`. See [Pages](ui.md#pages) |

## `windows`

| Member | Permission | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `open(id)` | none (the window is declared) | Opens one of the plugin's windows, or brings it to the front: `windowId`, `postMessage`, `onDidReceiveMessage`, `onDidClose`, `close()`. See [Windows](windows.md) |

## What every call shares

- Each call checks, at that moment: a signed-in account, the plugin not on the blocklist, the permission
  declared and allowed. A plugin that was running when one of these changed keeps running but gets nothing.
- Events reach a plugin only while it may receive them: turning a permission off stops them at once.
- Values cross between processes as JSON: functions and class instances do not, `Date`s become strings.

# The chat

What a plugin can know and do about the user's conversations. Each call names its permission; see
[API reference](api.md#chat) for the exact shapes.

## Turn events (`chat.events`)

```ts
vscode.breezell.chat.onDidStartTurn(turn => status.text = `Working (${turn.mode})`);
vscode.breezell.chat.onDidFinishTurn(turn => status.text = `${turn.outcome} in ${Math.round(turn.durationMs / 1000)} s`);
```

- A turn starts when the AI starts answering and finishes as `completed`, `error` or `stopped`. A turn
  waiting for the user's approval has not finished.
- `conversationId` in an event is stable per conversation in this window but is **not** the id
  `listConversations` uses; with `chat.read`, `conversationOfTurn(turnId)` gives that id.
- Events carry no content: the mode, the outcome and the duration. `chat.events` is normal: on unless the
  user turns it off.

## Reading conversations (`chat.read`)

```ts
const list = await vscode.breezell.chat.listConversations();           // most recently changed first
const open = list.find(c => c.current);
const conversation = open && await vscode.breezell.chat.getConversation(open.id);
for (const message of conversation?.messages ?? []) {
	if (message.kind === 'tool') { console.log(message.name, message.status, message.resultLength); }
}
vscode.breezell.chat.onDidChangeConversation(change => console.log(change.conversationId, change.activity));
```

- What the user sees in the chat of this workspace: their messages (with the memories recalled for
  each), replies with reasoning, each tool call with its parameters, status and result, and errors.
  Never Breezell's prompts, text only the model sees, hidden rows or other workspaces' conversations.
- A tool's parameters and result are cut at 20,000 characters (`resultLength` is the full length).
- `activity` is `idle`, `thinking`, `writing`, `runningTool`, `awaitingApproval` or `working`.
  `onDidChangeConversation` fires at most every 150 ms per conversation while it streams, with the
  reply being written in `streaming`.
- `show(id)` opens a conversation in Breezell's chat. `readInput()` (`chat.input`) gives what is typed in
  the chat box, its part before the caret, and the text of the last messages.

## Sending (`chat.send`)

```ts
const { conversationId } = await vscode.breezell.chat.send('Run the tests and fix what fails', {
	mode: 'agent',                                                 // normal, agent or plan
	model: { provider: 'openAICompatible', model: 'my-model' },     // one of models.list()
	attachments: ['src/app.ts', 'docs/screen.png'],                 // files of the workspace
});
await vscode.breezell.chat.stop(conversationId);                // stops the reply being written
```

- Without `conversationId` a new conversation starts. The call resolves once the message is in the
  conversation; the reply follows through `onDidChangeConversation`.
- The AI answers it as if the user had typed it, with the same tools, and it is billed the same way.
  At most 10 messages a minute per plugin; a busy conversation refuses it (`BreezellInvalidRequest`).
- `mode` and `model` are set as the user's pickers set them: in the conversation open in the chat the
  picker moves; another conversation keeps them as its own. Entanglement, Agent Teams and Dark Selene
  stay the user's choice. `model` must be one of `models.list()`.
- `attachments`: up to 10 files or folders of the workspace, by absolute path or relative to its first
  folder; images (png, jpg, gif, webp, up to 10 MB) go as images. Links, anything outside the workspace
  folders and what Breezell keeps from plugins are refused.
- `stop(id)` is not the user's Stop: `automated` messages may follow it.
- `approve(id)` / `reject(id)` (`chat.approve`) answer the tool call a conversation waits for. Leave
  approving to the user unless approving is what the plugin is for.

## Work over many turns

A plugin can keep a conversation going until something is done, as the [Goal](https://github.com/BreezellCode/BreezellCode/tree/main/plugins/examples/goal) example
does. All of this needs a Breezell newer than 1.4.41, and every call is checked against the sign-in and
the plugin's permissions: after a sign-out or a block it hears nothing more and can do nothing more.

```js
const { chat } = vscode.breezell;
await chat.holdDoneNotice(id);                               // no "done" sound for each turn
chat.onDidFinishTurn(async turn => {
	if (await chat.conversationOfTurn(turn.turnId) !== id) return;
	if (turn.outcome !== 'completed') { await chat.releaseDoneNotice(id); return; }   // stopped, or it failed
	const { backgroundCommands, usage } = await chat.getConversation(id);
	if (backgroundCommands?.willEnd) return;                   // its end starts a turn by itself
	if (done(usage)) { await chat.releaseDoneNotice(id, { announce: true }); return; }
	await chat.send('Go on with the tests', { conversationId: id, automated: true });
});
```

- **`automated`** is for a message the plugin sends on its own. It shows in the chat labelled with the
  plugin's name, and the AI is told the user did not type it. It does not count as the user reacting to the
  last turn and does not end up in their memories. Leave it out only for what a person asked to send.
- **Stop holds.** After the user presses Stop on the reply, an automated message fails with
  `BreezellStoppedByUser` until they write again. A message of theirs waiting in the queue goes first: yours
  fails with `BreezellInvalidRequest`, and the end of that turn is your next chance.
- **The done notice** can be held back, and comes once when released with `announce`. Errors still sound.
  A hold ends by itself on Stop, a sign-out, losing `chat.send`, a block, or the plugin stopping.
- **`backgroundCommands`** (`{ running, willEnd }`) says how many commands run in the background, and how
  many of them will end by themselves: servers and watchers do not. It is a count, not what they are.
- **`usage`** on a reply, on a conversation and on a `models.request` answer is the provider's numbers.
  Some providers count cache reads inside `inputTokens`. Subagents and checks that run beside a
  conversation are not in it, and `repliesWithoutUsage` says how many replies reported nothing.
- A turn's `outcome` is `completed`, `error` or `stopped`. A turn waiting for the user's approval has not
  finished, and a plugin should leave approving to the user.

## A message before it is sent

```js
vscode.breezell.chat.registerSendHandler(({ conversationId, text }) => {
	if (/sk-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}/.test(text)) {
		return { cancel: true, reason: 'This message seems to hold a secret key.' };
	}
	return { text: text.replace(/\bTODO\b/g, 'to do') };   // or nothing: as it is
});
```

Needs `chat.intercept`, one handler per plugin. It covers what the user sends (typed, queued, edited or a
follow-up they picked), not what Breezell or another plugin writes: a teammate's start, a plan's prompt,
`chat.send`. The message goes on through the usual send path, so its model, plan and billing are what they
would have been.

- It sees the text as it reads, with mentions written out (`@file.ts`), and `attachments`: the names of what goes with it. Attachments stay as they are.
- Context for the AI: answer `{ context: '...' }` (alone or with `text`), up to 20,000 characters, 50,000 from all
  plugins together. The AI reads it with the message and is told it came from your plugin; the user does not see
  it in the chat and `chat.read` does not show it. It stays in the conversation's history, and an edit of the
  message asks your handler again and replaces it.
- Stopped: the user is told by which plugin and why, and the text stays in the chat box.
- A command of the plugin's own: answer `{ cancel: true, handled: true }`. The box clears and nothing is said,
  so telling the user what happened is up to the plugin. Keep `reason` for an older Breezell, which takes it as stopped.
- Changed: what is sent is what shows in the bubble, and it must not be empty or over 400,000 characters.
- An answer later than 3 seconds, or a failure, passes the message on as it was, and all plugins together get
  at most 6 seconds.
- With several plugins they go in id order, each seeing what the one before made of it.

# Errors

Every failed `vscode.breezell` call throws an `Error` whose `name` is one of these. Check the name.

| `name` | When | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `BreezellNotSignedIn` | Nobody is signed in to Breezell | Wait for `account.onDidChangeSignIn`; do nothing meanwhile |
| `BreezellPermissionDenied` | The permission is not declared, or the user refused it or turned it off | Say what the plugin cannot do; offer `requestPermission` where it makes sense |
| `BreezellBlocked` | The plugin is on the market's blocklist | Nothing: every call fails until the user removes it |
| `BreezellNotAPlugin` | The extension has no `breezell` object in its `package.json` | Add it ([package.json](manifest.md)) |
| `BreezellInvalidRequest` | The call's arguments are wrong: no such conversation, a busy conversation, a model the picker does not offer, a refused attachment, a message too long | Fix the call; its message says what |
| `BreezellRateLimited` | Over a per-plugin limit: requests a minute, requests at a time, messages a minute | Wait and try again later; do not retry in a tight loop |
| `BreezellNoModel` | No chat model is selected and the request named none | Ask the user to pick a model, or pass `model` |
| `BreezellModelError` | The model failed: the provider's error, no answer in time, the API stopped answering, or no JSON when `responseFormat: 'json'` asked for it | Tell the user; retry once if it makes sense |
| `BreezellCancelled` | The request's cancellation token fired, or the extension host is going away | Nothing |
| `BreezellStoppedByUser` | An `automated` message after the user pressed Stop, before they wrote again | Wait for the user's next message |
| `BreezellPlanRequired` | `providers.listCustom()` for an account whose plan does not include Custom API | Say so; the user is not asked |

A plugin's own errors inside a tool (`invoke`), a send handler or a tool call handler never reach the user
as Breezell's: a tool's failure reaches the agent as a failed call, a handler's failure lets the message or
the call go on as it was.

# Getting started

From nothing to a plugin installed in your own Breezell. A plugin is a VS Code extension with a
`breezell` object in its `package.json` ([package.json](manifest.md)); everything VS Code extensions can
do, it can do, and `vscode.breezell` adds what is Breezell's ([API reference](api.md)).

**In Breezell**

Open **Breezell Console › Plugins › Develop**, fill in the id and name, choose a template (Pack,
Panel, AI command, Window or Minimal) and how to publish it (open or closed source), then pick a
folder. Open the new folder in a new window.

**From the command line** (Node.js 18 or later)

```bash
curl -O https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BreezellCode/BreezellCode/main/plugins/devkit/breezell-plugin.mjs
node breezell-plugin.mjs init my-plugin --id my-name.my-plugin --display-name "My Plugin" --template webview
cd my-plugin
npm install
```

Then open the folder in Breezell and press **F5**: the plugin runs in a development window.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `npm run build` / `npm run watch` | Bundle `src/extension.ts` into `dist/extension.js` with esbuild |
| `npm run typecheck` | TypeScript type check |
| `npm run validate` | Check `package.json` |
| `npm run package:open` | Pack as **open source**: the source and source maps ship in the package |
| `npm run package:closed` | Pack as **closed source**: minified code only (including the js and css in `media/`), no source, no source maps |
| `npm run submit -- --market <clone of the market>` | Add the package to the market (see "Publishing") |

## What a new plugin holds

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| `package.json` | The manifest: `breezell` (API version, permissions, source) and `contributes` |
| `src/extension.ts` | The plugin's code (`activate`, `deactivate`); not in a Pack |
| `types/breezell.d.ts` | The typings of `vscode.breezell`. Replace it with the market's newest copy when you need newer calls |
| `tools/breezell-plugin.mjs` | The devkit: `validate`, `pack`, `submit`. Replace it with the market's newest copy with the typings |
| `.agents/skills/breezell-plugin/` | The skill for an AI assistant, with these pages as references |
| `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` | What an AI assistant reads first |
| `.vscode/launch.json`, `tasks.json` | F5 runs the plugin in a development window |
| `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` | Shown on the plugin's market page; `i18n/` holds translations ([Translations](translations.md)) |

## Run it

1. `npm install`, then open the folder in Breezell.
2. Press **F5**. A development window opens with the plugin running; set breakpoints in `src/`.
3. Sign in to Breezell in that window: plugins run only while someone is signed in, and every
   `vscode.breezell` call fails with `BreezellNotSignedIn` otherwise.
4. Change the code, then **Developer: Restart Extension Host** (or reload the window) to run it again.
   `npm run watch` rebuilds as you save.

The plugin's log lines (`console.log`) are in **Help › Toggle Developer Tools** of the development window,
and Breezell's own lines about plugins start with `[BreezellPlugins]` in the **Window** output channel:
a declaration Breezell left out says why there.

## Check it

- `npm run validate` checks `package.json` the way Breezell reads it: permissions, every
  `contributes.breezell` entry, files it names. What it reports, Breezell would leave out.
- `npm run typecheck` checks the code against the typings.
- A permission the plugin uses must be declared; `validate` names the missing ones.

## Install it

`npm run package:open` (or `package:closed`) writes `<publisher.name>-<version>.vsix`. In Breezell,
**Plugins › Installed › Install local .vsix** installs it. A local plugin works the same as one from
the market; the user is told it was not reviewed.

## Before you publish

- [ ] `validate` and `typecheck` pass; the plugin does what it says with every permission turned off too
      (it says what it cannot do instead of failing silently).
- [ ] Only the permissions it needs, each explained in the README.
- [ ] It works in a remote (WSL, SSH) window: `"extensionKind": ["ui", "workspace"]`.
- [ ] It handles being signed out, blocked, and a call failing with each [error](errors.md) it can meet.
- [ ] The README says what it does, in English, with translations if you have them.
- [ ] Then [Publishing](publishing.md).
